items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall that a parabola can be defined as a set of points [MATH: (x,y)] equidistant from a line called the directrix and a point called the focus.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8ccfc6268231d35087042544b0896a57]

Content:
In this lesson, we will practice finding the coordinates of the focus of a parabola if we're given the equation of the parabola.

Content:
The first step is to write the parabola equation in its general form. For a horizontal parabola (like the one shown above), the general form is

Content:
[MATH: (y-k)^2 = 4p(x-h).]

Content:
From the general form, we can determine the coordinates of the vertex [MATH: (h,k)] and the value of the parameter [MATH: p,] and we can apply the following rule:

Content:
> The focus is located at a distance of [MATH: |p|] units away from the vertex, in the direction that the parabola opens.

Content:
That is to say:

Content:
- For a horizontal parabola, the focus has coordinates [MATH: (h + p, k).]
- For a vertical parabola, the focus has coordinates [MATH: (h, k + p).]

items.title: Calculating the Focus Given the Graph of a Horizontal Parabola

key_prerequisites.name: The Focus-Directrix Property of a Parabola

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the coordinates of the focus of the parabola shown below.
sections.readable_text:
Calculate the coordinates of the focus of the parabola shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/8796d1be466b9c27f184f16b12aa50e2]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The general equation of a horizontal parabola with vertex at [MATH: (h,k)] is given by

[MATH: (y - k)^2 = 4p(x-h),]

and the coordinates of the focus are [MATH: (h+p, k).]

From the diagram, we see that the vertex [MATH: (h,k) = (2,5).] Substituting this into the above, we get

[MATH: (y-5)^2=4p(x-2).]

The diagram shows that the parabola passes through the point [MATH: \left(11, 2\right).] Substituting [MATH: x= 11] and [MATH: y=2] into the above equation and solving for [MATH: p,] we get

[MATH: (2 − 5)^{2}|= 4p(11 − 2); 9|= 4p(9); p|= (1)/(4).]

Therefore, the coordinates of the focus are [MATH: \left(2+\dfrac{1}{4},5\right) = \left(\dfrac{9}{4},5\right).]

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the coordinates of the focus of the parabola [MATH: y^2 -12x - 14 y +49 = 0.]
sections.readable_text:
Calculate the coordinates of the focus of the parabola
[MATH: y^2 -12x - 14 y +49 = 0.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The general equation of a horizontal parabola with vertex at [MATH: (h,k)] is given by [MATH: (y - k)^2 = 4p(x - h)] and the coordinates of the focus are [MATH: (h + p, k).]

To rewrite the equation of the parabola in standard form, we need to group [MATH: y]-terms on the left-hand side of the equation and complete the square, as follows: [MATH: y^{2} − 12x − 14y + 49|= 0; y^{2} − 14y|= 12x − 49; (y − 7)^{2} − 49|= 12x − 49; (y − 7)^{2}|= 12x; (y − 7)^{2}|= 4(3)(x − 0)]

Therefore, [MATH: p = 3] and [MATH: (h, k) = \left(0, 7\right).]

Finally, the coordinates of the focus are [MATH: (h + p, k)|= (0 + 3, 7) = (3, 7).]
